description: One address's stablecoin transfer history on one chain, newest first, across the recent days and the archive: every token or one (token), what it sent, received or both (side), cursor-paginated. Use it for an address's transfers older than the recent window, or to page back through what it sent or received. Not for the chain-wide feed: get_recent_transactions. Not for who an address settles with: get_wallet_graph_walk. It reads as a caller without an API key: the newest 1000 transfers of the address on the side asked for — both is a listing of its own, its newest 1000 sent and received together, not 1000 of each (depth_limit 1000; with token, that token's rows among those 1000). Pass next_cursor back unchanged as cursor: a page may be short or even empty and still carry it — only a missing next_cursor ends the listing, and end says why (history_start: nothing older; depth_limit: older rows exist beyond the 1000). On an entry page (no cursor) total is the size of the whole listing, not of the 1000 you may page, and capped true makes it a lower bound (at least total). Without token: over 1000 or capped, say "the newest 1000 of <total>"; at most 1000, it is the whole listing, all of it yours to page. With token, total counts the token's rows: report that count, never "the newest 1000 of <total>" — the ones you may page are the token's among the newest 1000 of every token. null is unknown, not 0 (total_unavailable_reason archive_unavailable, archive_incomplete, counts_unavailable or timeout). coverage.missing names the days not served now (loading: on its way to the archive overnight); coverage.partial names archived days served without some rows (late_rows_withheld: rows written into the day after it was archived, served after the next nightly load). On Solana coverage is incomplete (coverage.scope incomplete, coverage.note): only watched accounts and addresses looked up on demand are indexed, so a transfer missing there is not evidence. Heavy read: under load it answers busy or timeout — retry with backoff; timeout also comes briefly during the nightly archive move (03:30–05:00 UTC). No auth; 1200 requests/min shared by all tools. Plain on-chain Transfer facts, no scoring.

address.description: The address whose transfers to list. The address in its network's own spelling: 0x… for EVM chains, T… for Tron, base58 for Solana. The answer writes it in the spelling of chain_id (address) and echoes what you sent (requested_address); address_respelled true means your spelling belongs to another kind of chain than chain_id (a T… address asked about an EVM chain, a 0x… address asked about Tron) — answered about the same bytes there, not refused, and the same owner only for a plain key account.

chain.description: Chain, in any of four spellings: the id (8453 Base — default for 0x addresses; a T… address defaults to Tron and a base58 one to Solana, 1 Ethereum, 10 Optimism, 42161 Arbitrum, 56 BNB Chain, 728126428 Tron, -1 Solana), the same id as a string, the network slug (base, ethereum, optimism, arbitrum, bnb-chain, tron, solana) or its CAIP-2 id (eip155:1, solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp). Surrounding whitespace, a leading + and leading zeros are ignored, a JSON number counts by its value (1.0 is 1), slugs and CAIP-2 ids match in any letter case, and an empty, blank or null chain is no chain at all. Anything else (hex, a decimal fraction, a zero-padded CAIP-2 reference) is refused, and so is a network this scanner knows but does not index — by name, never with an empty listing. The answer is about ONE chain: chain_id says which, chain_source says how it was chosen (explicit|default|address_form) and chains_with_data lists where else this address has data — read it before concluding, then ask again with chain set

cursor.description: next_cursor (with dir older) or prev_cursor (with dir newer) of a page of this same address, chain, side and token, passed back unchanged; any other cursor is refused

dir.description: older (the default: with next_cursor, toward older rows) or newer (with prev_cursor, back toward newer ones). Rows are newest first on every page; newer without a cursor starts at the oldest row the depth lets you read

limit.description: Max rows, 1..200 (default 25). A value outside that range is refused, as REST refuses it

side.description: payer (what the address sent), recipient (what it received) or both (the default). A burn is listed under its payer only, a self-transfer once. Each side is a listing of its own, with its own cursors and its own newest 1000

token.description: A registry symbol of that chain (USDC, USDT, USDC.e; any letter case) to list one stablecoin; absent: every token, not the chain's default one. A symbol the chain does not enable is refused

name: get_transfer_history
